requirements.title: Original files are never deleted, edited, or truncated
requirements.text: The app never deletes, edits, or truncates an original archive file.
requirements.sourceText: The app never deletes or edits original files.
requirements.testNotes: Static guard plus the read-only integration test prove the invariant.
requirements.notes: This is the core promise. The quarantine exception must not weaken it.

requirements.title: Only the duplicate quarantine mover may move or rename an original file
requirements.text: The only operation that may move or rename an original file is the duplicate quarantine mover, after explicit confirmation. Every other source operation is read-only.
requirements.sourceText: Original files are never moved, renamed, edited, or deleted.
requirements.testNotes: Covers the mover and the confirmed cleanup service.
requirements.notes: The README, acceptance row 2, scan contract, other-files contract, and security review still state the old absolute rule.

requirements.title: Every non-quarantine source read opens the original file read-only
requirements.text: Scan, metadata, thumbnails, hashing, validation, media playback, and replication open source files read-only. Only the quarantine mover may open a source file for a rename.
requirements.sourceText: Source files are opened with read access only, except by the quarantine mover.
requirements.testNotes: Tests exercise the readers; none asserts the open mode directly.
requirements.notes: A direct open-mode assertion would make this invariant stronger than a code review.

requirements.title: The quarantine mover is the only source write path
requirements.text: The quarantine mover is the only source write path. It is reachable only through the confirmed cleanup operation, and every other source write is rejected by the guard.
requirements.sourceText: The read-only guard allows only the quarantine mover to rename source files.
requirements.testNotes: Covers the mover and the cleanup handler; the static guard is separate.
requirements.notes: The security review allowlist does not yet name the quarantine mover.

requirements.title: The read-only guard fails on unreviewed write APIs
requirements.text: The read-only guard fails the quality gate when a direct filesystem write API appears outside the reviewed allowlist. The allowlist names every permitted writer and is reviewed with the security review.
requirements.sourceText: A static read-only guard fails the build if direct filesystem write calls appear outside the reviewed allowlist.
requirements.testNotes: The guard is the gate itself; it is not a Vitest test.
requirements.notes: The guard is defense-in-depth, not the primary runtime control.

requirements.title: The DB worker is the only SQLite writer
requirements.text: The DB worker is the only SQLite writer for the app database and the active catalog. Main and renderer never open SQLite directly.
requirements.sourceText: The DB worker is the single SQLite writer for both databases. The main process never opens SQLite directly.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover the worker protocol and catalog registry; dependency-cruiser enforces the import boundary.
requirements.notes: The boundary is also enforced by .dependency-cruiser.cjs.

requirements.title: No IPC contract accepts a source path for writing
requirements.text: No IPC contract accepts a source path for writing outside the quarantine operation. Renderer requests use catalog IDs, never arbitrary filesystem paths.
requirements.sourceText: No replication IPC accepts a source path for writing.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover sender trust and contract shapes; no single test scans every IPC contract for source paths.
requirements.notes: A contract-wide scan could become a traceability check later.

requirements.title: The source catalog database may be written; source archive files may not
requirements.text: The app writes the source archive's catalog database and app-managed caches. It does not write source archive files, except for the quarantine mover.
requirements.sourceText: Source files remain unmodified; only the source archive's catalog database is written.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover read-only database connections and the source index.
requirements.notes: This is the wording that lets replication write metadata without weakening the source-file promise.

requirements.title: Scans exclude app-managed directories
requirements.text: Scans exclude both `.memorylane` and `.memorylane_quarantine` so app-managed data is never cataloged as archive content.
requirements.sourceText: Scans exclude `.memorylane`; `.memorylane_quarantine` is also excluded.
requirements.testNotes: The enumerator test creates a quarantine folder and asserts it is skipped.

requirements.title: Backups and validation read source data read-only
requirements.text: Backups and validation open source databases and files read-only. Backups use SQLite's online backup API, not a live file copy.
requirements.sourceText: Backups open both databases read-only and use SQLite's backup API.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover the read-only connection and backup runner.

requirements.title: Duplicate groups are exact full-SHA-256 groups
requirements.text: Duplicate groups contain only files with the same full SHA-256 and list every present copy.
requirements.sourceText: Duplicate files are detected by SHA-256 and shown with all locations.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover exact grouping and the cleanup domain.

requirements.title: The keeper is a verified backup copy first, then the oldest copy
requirements.text: The keeper is a verified backup copy first. If several copies are covered, the oldest covered copy wins; otherwise the oldest copy wins. Remaining tiebreakers are oldest modified, shallower and shorter path, shorter name, then lower file ID.
requirements.sourceText: The keeper is a verified backup copy first. If several copies are covered, the oldest covered copy wins, then oldest modified, then shallower and shorter path, then shorter name, then lower file ID.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover the keeper comparator and covered-copy promotion.

requirements.title: Coverage is a preference, not an eligibility gate
requirements.text: Coverage is a preference, not an eligibility gate. A group with no covered copy remains eligible and is shown with a warning that the quarantine folder is not a backup until it is copied elsewhere.
requirements.sourceText: Verified backup coverage is not required. A group with no covered copy is eligible, but the confirmation and completion screens warn that the quarantine folder is not a backup until it is copied elsewhere.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover uncovered-group eligibility and the warning UI.

requirements.title: The duplicates view shows KEEP/MOVE and SKIP with a reason
requirements.text: The duplicates view shows KEEP and MOVE badges for eligible groups, and SKIP with the reason for every group that fails a gate.
requirements.sourceText: The page shows KEEP / MOVE badges for eligible groups and SKIP plus the reason for groups that fail a gate.
requirements.testNotes: Component and E2E tests cover keeper badges and skip reasons.

requirements.title: The confirmation states the full consequence
requirements.text: The confirmation shows the counts, keeper rule, quarantine path, skip rules, required acknowledgement, and how many groups have no verified backup.
requirements.sourceText: The confirmation requires an explicit acknowledgement and reports how many groups have no verified backup.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover the dialog and the required acknowledgement.

requirements.title: Progress shows moved files, bytes, current path, and cancel
requirements.text: Progress shows files and bytes moved, the current path, and a cancel action that stops after the current file.
requirements.sourceText: Progress shows files/bytes moved, current path, and cancel-after-current.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover progress state and cancel-after-current.

requirements.title: Completion states the manual next steps
requirements.text: Completion shows moved and skipped totals and the manual next steps: back up the quarantine folder, remove it, and rescan.
requirements.sourceText: Completion shows moved/skipped totals and the manual next steps: back up the quarantine folder, remove it, rescan.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover completion state and totals.

requirements.title: The mover verifies before and after the move
requirements.text: The mover re-hashes the source immediately before the move and the quarantined copy immediately after. A mismatch restores the source and journals the restore; if the restore fails, the run aborts.
requirements.sourceText: The mover re-checks the keeper and every candidate with full SHA-256 immediately before the same-volume move. After the move it hashes the quarantined copy again. A mismatch is moved back to the source path and journaled; if the restore fails, the run aborts.
requirements.testNotes: The mover test restores a file when the quarantined copy fails verification.

requirements.title: The mover never moves the last eligible copy
requirements.text: The mover never moves the last eligible copy. Every group retains one keeper.
requirements.sourceText: One keeper per group; never move the last copy.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover keeper selection and the last-copy guard.

requirements.title: The mover skips unsafe or ambiguous candidates
requirements.text: The mover skips and reports groups with active date overrides on non-keeper copies, multiple overrides, hard links, empty files, files under 1 KB, changed or missing files, outside-root paths, or cross-volume renames.
requirements.sourceText: Skip groups with active date overrides on non-keeper copies, multiple overrides, hard links, empty files, files under 1 KB, changed or missing files, outside-root paths, or cross-volume renames.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover changed, missing, hard-link, and outside-root cases.

requirements.title: Every move is auditable and the quarantine is never deleted
requirements.text: Every move writes a manifest entry, a journal line, and a `cleanup_moves` audit row. The app never deletes the quarantine folder.
requirements.sourceText: Write a journal line for every move. The app never deletes the quarantine folder.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover the manifest, journal, audit rows, and migration.

requirements.title: A move batch updates the catalog and audit state
requirements.text: After a move batch, the moved catalog rows are deleted, `cleanup_moves` keeps the audit record, duplicate groups are rebuilt, and destination adoption counters are refreshed.
requirements.sourceText: Moves are applied to the catalog in batches. The moved files rows are deleted, cleanup_moves keeps the audit record, duplicate groups are rebuilt, and destination adoption counters are refreshed.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover row deletion, audit rows, duplicate rebuild, and counters.

requirements.title: A rescan does not report moved files as missing
requirements.text: After a cleanup, a rescan does not report the moved files as missing because their catalog rows were removed with the move.
requirements.sourceText: A rescan therefore does not treat the moved files as missing.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover catalog row deletion; no dedicated rescan-after-cleanup E2E yet.
requirements.notes: This is a good candidate for a new integration test.

requirements.title: Cancel, failure, and interruption leave an auditable run
requirements.text: Cancel stops after the current file. A cancelled, failed, or interrupted run remains auditable through its journal, manifest, and cleanup run record.
requirements.sourceText: Cancel stops after the current file. The run remains auditable if it is cancelled, fails, or is interrupted by an app restart.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover cancel and interrupted state.

requirements.title: The Move button is live; there is no preview-only phase
requirements.text: The Move button is live in the first release. There is no preview-only phase and no settings toggle.
requirements.sourceText: The Move button is live in the first release; no read-only preview phase and no settings toggle.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover the live button and confirmation.

requirements.title: No user-defined protected folders in the first release
requirements.text: The first release does not support user-defined protected folders. System paths `.memorylane` and `.memorylane_quarantine` are always excluded.
requirements.sourceText: Scope: all eligible groups; no user-defined protected folders.
requirements.testNotes: No test: explicit non-goal.

requirements.title: No history or restore UI in the first release
requirements.text: The first release has no history or restore UI. Restore is a manual copy back plus a rescan.
requirements.sourceText: Restore manually by copying files back and rescanning. History/restore is phase 2.
requirements.testNotes: No test: explicit non-goal.

requirements.title: No automatic quarantine removal
requirements.text: The app never deletes the quarantine folder and never removes quarantine content automatically.
requirements.sourceText: The app never deletes the quarantine folder. Journal and DB audit; no automatic quarantine removal.
requirements.testNotes: No test: explicit non-goal.

requirements.title: Drive identity is stable and independent of the drive letter
requirements.text: A drive is identified by a stable volume identity, not by its drive letter. The catalog validates the identity on open.
requirements.sourceText: The app must identify a drive independently of its drive letter.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover identity and drive listing.

requirements.title: A changed drive letter requires confirmation
requirements.text: A changed drive letter is recognized by identity and requires explicit confirmation before the catalog root is updated. It is never treated as a new archive silently.
requirements.sourceText: If the same drive is reconnected with a different drive letter, ask the user to confirm before updating the catalog root.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover changed-letter handling.

requirements.title: Each archive drive owns its catalog and cache
requirements.text: Each archive drive owns a self-contained `.memorylane/catalog.db` and app-managed cache, separate from original folders. The PC backup is a safety copy, not the owner.
requirements.sourceText: Each archive drive has its own independent SQLite database stored on that drive, separate from original folders.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover catalog creation and connections.

requirements.title: Scan starts only on explicit user action
requirements.text: A scan starts only on explicit user action. After interruption, resume is explicit; the app never resumes automatically.
requirements.sourceText: The user explicitly starts the initial scan with a Start scan action. Do not automatically resume.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover start, pause, resume, and UI state.

requirements.title: Scan runs four stages and browsing unlocks after catalog
requirements.text: A scan runs four ordered stages: catalog, metadata, thumbnails, hashes. Browsing unlocks after the catalog stage; later stages continue in the background.
requirements.sourceText: Use a staged workflow: catalog, metadata, thumbnails, hashes. Do not require all stages to finish before browsing.
requirements.testNotes: Tests assert the four stages and stage order.

requirements.title: Pause persists progress and resume continues
requirements.text: Pause finishes the current file or batch, persists per-stage progress, and stops scheduling new work. Resume continues from that saved progress without recopying completed work.
requirements.sourceText: Pause completes the current file or batch, persists progress, and stops scheduling new work. Resume continues from saved per-stage progress.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover pause/resume and persisted session state.

requirements.title: Close or disconnect interrupts safely
requirements.text: App close or drive disconnect marks the scan interrupted, preserves completed work, and requires explicit resume after reconnect.
requirements.sourceText: If the app closes or the drive disconnects, stop safely, persist completed work, and require explicit resume.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover interruption and recovery.

requirements.title: Incremental scan detects new, changed, missing, and moved
requirements.text: An incremental scan adds new files, refreshes changed files, marks missing files, and proposes moved candidates. Missing files stay in the catalog.
requirements.sourceText: A later scan detects new, modified, missing, and moved files; missing files are not removed automatically.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover incremental reports and moved candidates.

requirements.title: Scan report counts new, changed, missing, and moved
requirements.text: A completed scan reports newFiles, changedFiles, missingFiles, and movedCandidates. The report is null until the scan completes.
requirements.sourceText: ScanReport has newFiles, changedFiles, missingFiles, movedCandidates; report is non-null only when complete.
requirements.testNotes: Tests assert report shape and completion state.

requirements.title: Large files use a quick fingerprint until a full hash is needed
requirements.text: Files over the quick-hash threshold use a sampled fingerprint only until a full SHA-256 is required by a duplicate, move, replication, or validation decision. Existing full hashes are reused.
requirements.sourceText: Large files without a same-size peer use a sampled fingerprint; full SHA-256 is computed when a duplicate/move candidate or replication/validation needs it.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover quick hashing and full hashes.

requirements.title: Metadata extraction is versioned and refreshable
requirements.text: Metadata extraction uses ExifTool as the primary extractor with dependency-free fallbacks. Each success records the extractor version; stale metadata is reported and refreshed by an incremental scan.
requirements.sourceText: ExifTool is primary with dependency-free fallbacks; successful extraction records the extractor version.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover extraction and metadata refresh.
requirements.notes: Version 2 re-resolves filesystem dates on the next incremental scan; no file rehash is required.

requirements.title: Dates preserve provenance and never invent a value
requirements.text: Every resolved date preserves precision, the original extracted value, provenance, and confidence. Embedded metadata wins; without a usable embedded date, the older non-placeholder filesystem date is used. A missing or suspicious date is shown as unavailable or flagged, never invented.
requirements.sourceText: Resolve the best date, preserve precision, original value, source, and confidence; embedded metadata wins. When none is usable, use the older of filesystem created and modified, ignoring placeholder and future dates.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover metadata priority, partial dates, suspicious values, and the older filesystem fallback.
requirements.notes: The metadata extractor version was bumped so the next incremental scan re-resolves existing filesystem dates.

requirements.title: Manual dates use year or year-month precision
requirements.text: Manual date assignment supports individual and bulk edits at year or year-month precision. It never invents a day, updates catalog metadata only, and preserves the extracted date for reversal.
requirements.sourceText: Manual assignment accepts year or year/month; never invent a day; preserve the extracted date.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover manual date precision and clearing.

requirements.title: Browsing and scanning stay responsive at 100k+ items
requirements.text: Browsing uses a virtualized grid, lazy thumbnails, and indexed queries. Visible thumbnails preempt bulk work. The 100k and 200k query budgets remain green.
requirements.sourceText: Use a virtualized grid, lazy thumbnails, indexed queries, and viewport-priority thumbnails; 100k/200k query passes.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover query budgets and thumbnail priority.

requirements.title: One chronological timeline for photos and videos
requirements.text: Photos and videos share one chronological timeline with all/photos/videos filters. Ordering is resolved_date DESC, then file_id DESC; undated items sort last.
requirements.sourceText: Photos and videos are grouped together in one chronological timeline; filters all/photos/videos; ordering resolved_date DESC, file_id DESC; undated last.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover ordering and filters.

requirements.title: Year/month navigation and date grouping honor precision
requirements.text: Year and month navigation anchor the timeline, and date-grouped sections use the stored precision: day, month, year, then Date unavailable.
requirements.sourceText: Navigation by year and month; date grouping uses stored precision; Date unavailable is a trailing section.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover anchors and grouping.

requirements.title: The grid is virtualized and thumbnails are lazy
requirements.text: The grid renders only visible rows and loads thumbnails lazily. Visible items preempt nearby and bulk thumbnail work.
requirements.sourceText: Use a virtualized grid; load thumbnails lazily; prioritize visible items.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover virtualization and thumbnail priority.

requirements.title: The viewer supports photos, videos, and filter-aware navigation
requirements.text: The viewer displays photos at fit/100% and plays videos natively. Previous/next carries the active filter and density, and Escape returns to the same filtered grid.
requirements.sourceText: Photos display in-app; videos play in-app; previous/next carries the active filter and density; Escape returns to the filtered grid.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover viewer navigation and playback states.

requirements.title: Item details and missing states retain catalog context
requirements.text: The viewer shows path, folder, timestamps, extracted metadata, position, previous/next, and the media URL. Missing or failed media keeps the catalog details and shows a clear unavailable state.
requirements.sourceText: Details include path, folder, timestamps, metadata, position, previous/next, media URL; missing files keep details with mediaUrl null.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover details and missing states.

requirements.title: Media URLs use catalog IDs and byte ranges
requirements.text: `ml-media:` resolves catalog IDs, never renderer paths. It serves only present files, supports byte ranges and the cataloged MIME type, and returns 404 for missing files.
requirements.sourceText: Resolve files by ID, never accept a renderer path; serve only present files; support byte ranges and MIME; missing returns 404.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover ID resolution, ranges, and missing files.

requirements.title: Thumbnails are cached, deduplicated, and failure-safe
requirements.text: Thumbnails serve from cache when ready, otherwise generate on demand with interactive priority. In-flight work is deduplicated; failures return 404 so the grid shows a placeholder.
requirements.sourceText: Serve a ready cache entry; otherwise generate on demand with interactive priority; deduplicate in-flight work; failures return 404.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover cache hits, deduplication, and failures.

requirements.title: HEIC previews are generated on demand and cached
requirements.text: HEIC/HEIF images generate a JPEG preview on demand in a worker thread, cache it under `.memorylane/cache/previews`, and fall back to external open on failure.
requirements.sourceText: HEIC/HEIF images generate a JPEG preview in a worker, cache it, and fall back to external open on failure.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover preview generation and failure fallback.

requirements.title: WMV/3GP and failed playback use a cached MP4 proxy
requirements.text: WMV, 3GP, and failed direct video playback use a cached H.264/AAC MP4 proxy. A source change invalidates the cache; failure offers retry and external open.
requirements.sourceText: WMV/3GP and failed direct playback use a cached H.264/AAC MP4; source changes invalidate; failure offers retry/external open.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover proxy generation and failure states.

requirements.title: The cache is disposable and never affects originals
requirements.text: The generated cache lives on the external drive, is excluded from the PC database backup, and is disposable. Clearing it never changes an original file or a catalog row.
requirements.sourceText: Cache lives on the external drive, is excluded from PC DB backup, is disposable/regenerable, and clearing never affects originals or catalog entries.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover cache clearing and regeneration.

requirements.title: Health summary reports duplicates, missing, moved, and validation state
requirements.text: The health summary reports duplicate groups, missing files, moved candidates, missing duplicates, and the current validation state in one place.
requirements.sourceText: HealthSummary covers duplicate groups, missing files, moved candidates, and validation state.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover the summary and handlers.

requirements.title: Duplicate detection uses exact full SHA-256 only
requirements.text: Duplicate groups contain only files with the same full SHA-256. A sampled quick fingerprint is never duplicate evidence; a large file is fully hashed when another present or fully hashed missing file shares its size.
requirements.sourceText: Exact SHA-256 duplicates across all present catalog files; sampled quick fingerprints are never duplicate evidence.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover exact grouping and full-hash promotion.

requirements.title: Duplicate groups list every copy with its context
requirements.text: Every duplicate group lists each present copy with path, folder, media metadata, date, thumbnail, missing state, filesystem timestamps, verified-backup state, and active date-override state.
requirements.sourceText: Each HealthFile includes path, folder, media metadata, date, thumbnail URL, missing state, duplicate state, filesystem timestamps, verified-backup state, and active date-override state.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover group members and UI badges.

requirements.title: Duplicate groups are ordered by total bytes
requirements.text: Duplicate groups are ordered by total bytes descending, then group id. Page totals include the excess bytes for every eligible group.
requirements.sourceText: Group ordering is total bytes descending, then group id; page totals include excess bytes for eligible groups.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover ordering and excess totals.

requirements.title: Duplicate groups are rebuilt after catalog changes
requirements.text: Duplicate groups are rebuilt after scan finalize, after validation completes, and after catalog changes that can affect duplicates. Quick fingerprints never enter the group.
requirements.sourceText: duplicate_groups and duplicate_members are rebuilt after scan finalize, on duplicate query, and after validation completes.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover rebuild points.

requirements.title: Missing files stay cataloged
requirements.text: A file missing from its recorded path is marked missing and stays in the catalog. It is never removed automatically.
requirements.sourceText: Files no longer present are marked missing and are never removed from the catalog automatically.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover missing marking and preservation.

requirements.title: Missing files can be disregarded and restored
requirements.text: A missing file can be disregarded, which records `dismissed_at`, dismisses its pending move suggestions, and keeps the catalog row. Restore clears the dismissal. Neither action changes a source or backup file.
requirements.sourceText: Disregarding records dismissed_at, dismisses pending move suggestions, keeps the catalog row, and never changes source or backup files. Restore clears dismissed_at.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover dismiss and restore.

requirements.title: Missing lists page and select across the full result
requirements.text: The missing and disregarded lists are offset-paged in the UI and return the IDs of every matching file so Select all covers more than the visible page. The disregarded list is newest-first. Dismiss and restore accept up to 50,000 IDs per request.
requirements.sourceText: The missing list is offset-paged in the UI, includes fileIds for every matching file, and dismiss/restore accept up to 50,000 ids. The disregarded list is ordered by dismissed_at descending.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover offset paging, newest-first disregarded order, and bulk selection across pages.

requirements.title: Moved candidates are paginated and batch-confirmed
requirements.text: A moved candidate records old path, new path, size, and SHA-256. The list is paginated, confirm accepts at most 500 candidates per request, and dismiss accepts up to 50,000.
requirements.sourceText: A pending moved candidate contains old path, new path, size, and SHA-256. The list is paginated; confirm is capped at 500, dismiss at 50,000.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover candidate shape and paging.

requirements.title: Confirming a move rechecks and updates the catalog
requirements.text: Confirming a move rechecks the new path and hash in the main process, deletes the newly discovered duplicate row, updates the original catalog row to the new path, clears missing state, and confirms the candidate.
requirements.sourceText: Confirm flow rechecks the new path and hash in the main process, deletes the newly discovered duplicate row, updates the original row, clears missing state, and confirms the candidate.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover recheck and catalog update.

requirements.title: Dismissing a move keeps the file missing
requirements.text: Dismissing a moved candidate keeps the file missing and marks the candidate dismissed without changing the catalog path.
requirements.sourceText: Dismissing keeps the file missing and marks the candidate dismissed.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover dismissal state.

requirements.title: Missing-duplicate cleanup removes catalog rows only
requirements.text: Missing-duplicate cleanup removes only eligible missing catalog rows that have a complete full SHA-256 and a present file with the same hash and size. Source and destination files are never touched, and adoption counters are refreshed.
requirements.sourceText: Cleanup removes only eligible missing catalog rows with a full hash and a present same-hash/size peer; source and destination files are never touched.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover eligibility and catalog-only removal.

requirements.title: Missing-duplicate preview reports risk and pending moves
requirements.text: The missing-duplicate preview reports how many candidates have pending move suggestions, verified backup replicas, and active date overrides before cleanup.
requirements.sourceText: The preview reports pending move suggestions, verified backup replicas, and active date overrides.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover preview counts and warnings.

requirements.title: Validation has independently selectable levels
requirements.text: Validation offers four independently selectable levels: existence, metadata, hash, and metadataRefresh.
requirements.sourceText: Validation supports existence, metadata, hash, and metadataRefresh levels, independently selectable.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover level selection and state.

requirements.title: Validation covers the whole catalog and stores per-file results
requirements.text: Validation covers the whole catalog. Total checks equal the file count multiplied by the selected levels, and every result is stored per session, level, and file.
requirements.sourceText: Scope is the whole catalog; total checks = file count × selected levels; results are stored per session/level/file.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover totals and result storage.

requirements.title: Hash validation records mismatches and updates the stored hash
requirements.text: Hash validation recomputes SHA-256, records a mismatch, and updates the stored hash to the actual value.
requirements.sourceText: hash recomputes SHA-256; mismatch is recorded and the stored hash is updated to the actual value.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover mismatch and hash update.

requirements.title: Metadata refresh preserves manual date overrides
requirements.text: Metadata refresh re-extracts metadata through ExifTool, writes metadata and extracted dates, and preserves every active manual date override.
requirements.sourceText: metadataRefresh re-extracts metadata through ExifTool, writes metadata and extracted dates, and preserves manual date overrides.
requirements.testNotes: The scan-stage metadata test proves an active manual override survives a metadata save; the validation metadataRefresh path calls the same saveMetadata handler.

requirements.title: Validation marks missing files without deleting them
requirements.text: A missing validation result marks the file state as missing and inserts a `missing_files` row without deleting the catalog row.
requirements.sourceText: missing results mark files.state = 'missing' and insert missing_files.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover missing result persistence.

requirements.title: Validation pauses, resumes, and recovers
requirements.text: Validation supports pause, resume, shutdown-pause, stale-session recovery, and explicit failure states.
requirements.sourceText: Pause, resume, shutdown-pause, stale-session recovery, and failure states are supported.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover pause/resume and recovery.

requirements.title: Validation reports every outcome
requirements.text: The validation report counts verified, missing, metadata changed, hash mismatch, metadata updated, and unreadable results, with start and finish times.
requirements.sourceText: Report counts verified, missing, metadata changed, hash mismatch, metadata updated, unreadable, start and finish time.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover report counts.

requirements.title: Health actions never change original files
requirements.text: Missing, moved, duplicate, missing-duplicate, and validation actions change catalog metadata only. They never move, rename, edit, or delete a source file.
requirements.sourceText: No source file is moved, renamed, edited, or deleted by health actions.
requirements.testNotes: The read-only guard test covers the source-write boundary.
requirements.notes: The quarantine mover is the one source-moving exception; see ML-SAFE-002.

requirements.title: Health UI exposes Missing, Duplicates, and Validation tabs
requirements.text: The Health route exposes Missing files, Duplicates, and Validation tabs, including empty, loading, error, and populated states.
requirements.sourceText: The /health route has Missing files, Duplicates, and Validation tabs with their states.
requirements.testNotes: Tests cover tabs and states.

requirements.title: Validation is exclusive with scan and cleanup

conflicts.title: The read-only promise and the quarantine mover disagree

claims.text: It never moves, renames, edits, or deletes the originals.
Original files are never moved, renamed, edited, or deleted.
source files are never moved or modified.
The app never moves, renames, edits, or deletes an original.
No module is allowed to write, rename, truncate, or delete an original archive file.

contradictedBy.text: This is the only Memory Lane action that moves archive files. It never deletes them.
The single exception is the explicit duplicate quarantine, which moves only confirmed duplicate copies into X:\.memorylane_quarantine. Nothing is deleted or edited.

conflicts.proposedResolution: Adopt the product-spec wording: originals are never deleted or edited; the quarantine mover is the only operation that may move an eligible duplicate copy, after explicit confirmation. Update README, acceptance row 2, scan contract, other-files contract, and security review. Add ADR-0010 for the quarantine exception.
conflicts.recommendation: Approve the exception and update all five stale claims. Do not remove the quarantine feature; it is implemented and tested.
conflicts.decision: Adopt the product-spec wording; update README, acceptance row 2, scan.md, other-files.md, and security review; add ADR-0010.

conflicts.title: The security review does not list the quarantine mover

claims.text: The read-only guard allowlist names catalog locks, thumbnails, HEIC previews, video proxies, cache deletion, and databases/logs/backups. It does not name the quarantine mover.

contradictedBy.text: Scans exclude .memorylane_quarantine; the read-only guard allows only the quarantine mover to rename source files.
check-read-only.mjs fails the quality gate if direct filesystem write APIs appear outside the reviewed cache/lock/backup/quarantine allowlist.

conflicts.proposedResolution: Add a 'Duplicate quarantine extension' section to the security review. Name the quarantine mover in the allowlist, state the re-hash/restore guardrail, and confirm the source is read-only outside that adapter.
conflicts.recommendation: Approve and update the security review before the next release sign-off.
conflicts.decision: Add a Duplicate quarantine extension section and allowlist the quarantine mover.

conflicts.title: The quarantine feature is implemented but not indexed or accepted

contradictedBy.text: The docs index does not list duplicate-quarantine-plan.md.
The README documentation table does not list the quarantine plan.
There is no ADR-0010 for the quarantine exception.
The roadmap does not mention duplicate quarantine.
The acceptance criteria do not include quarantine.

conflicts.proposedResolution: Add the plan to docs/README.md and the README docs table; add it to the roadmap's delivered state; add ADR-0010; add quarantine acceptance rows; link the plan from the health contract.
conflicts.recommendation: Approve the documentation set before calling the feature implemented in the release record.
conflicts.decision: Add ADR-0010, docs index entries, the README docs table, roadmap state, and a post-v0.1 acceptance section.

catalog schema is version 6 after the video-frame-rate and ...

conflicts.decision: Update scan.md and settings.md to schema 12; add a docs check that reads the migration folder.

conflicts.title: The replication matrix names schema 8, but the catalog is at 12

claims.text: R-01 says fresh catalogs migrate to the current schema (8).
R-02 says existing schema 6 catalogs migrate without data loss.

conflicts.proposedResolution: Change R-01 to say "the current catalog schema" without a number, or update it to 12. Keep R-02 as the historical schema 6 migration path, because it describes a real upgrade from an older catalog.
conflicts.recommendation: Approve the wording change when batch 4 is approved. Do not change the migration tests; they already use CATALOG_SCHEMA_VERSION.
conflicts.decision: Approved: R-01 now says the current catalog schema; R-02 keeps schema 6 as the historical migration path.

conflicts.title: The product spec calls the PC backup catalog-only, but the contract backs up app.db too

claims.text: The SQLite catalog should be backed up automatically; the PC backup is an additional copy of the catalog only.
The SQLite catalog is backed up to the PC every 15 minutes while open and on close.

contradictedBy.text: Back up both `catalog.db` and `app.db` with the SQLite online backup API.
`catalog.db` and `app.db` are backed up with the SQLite online backup API.

conflicts.proposedResolution: Update product-specification.md section 8 and section 17 to say both SQLite databases (catalog.db and app.db) are backed up, while the generated cache remains excluded. Keep the user-facing name 'catalog backup'.
conflicts.recommendation: Approve the contract/ADR behavior and update the two stale product-spec sentences. Do not stop backing up app.db; it holds drive registration and backup history.
conflicts.decision: Approved: update product-specification section 8 and section 17 to name both SQLite databases; keep the generated cache excluded.
